explanation: Loss of a resting K+ leak or subthreshold K+ conductance (Kir2.x, K2P TASK/TREK, Kv7) raises input resistance and depolarises rest (hypothesised)
assumes: The conductance exists in layer II/III pyramidal neurons at P13-17 and is reduced by neuronal Wwox loss
discriminating_measurement: Voltage clamp: Ba2+-sensitive, XE991-sensitive and TTX-resistant leak current and its reversal potential in knockout vs wild type; I-V slope near rest; effect of the blocker in wild type should phenocopy the knockout, and add little in the knockout
agents_or_tools: Tool compounds: barium at low concentration (Kir), XE991 (Kv7 blocker, no database id verified); candidate agonist-type tools to restore: Kv7 openers such as retigabine (id not verified)
action: Block in wild type to phenocopy; open in knockout to rescue
system_and_stage: Mouse neocortical slice, P13-17 (proposed); Kv7/Kir roles transferred from other cortical preparations
benefit_sought: Rescue of resting potential and burst incidence by a restoring tool
counter_evidence: In an HCN1 gain-of-function DEE mouse, retigabine increased spiking (single origin, ECoG, in vivo), so opening Kv7 is not safe to assume protective
falsifier: If the blocker-sensitive current is equal in knockout and wild type, H1 fails; a failed rescue alone does not refute it
depth_and_source: Transferred: abstract only (PMID 36300716); mechanism inferred from general biophysics, not read

explanation: Increased HCN (Ih) availability or surface expression (HCN1 trafficking via TRIP8b, or altered gating) explains larger sag, rebound and a depolarised rest (inferred)
assumes: Sag and rebound in the knockout are Ih-mediated (ZD7288-sensitive); Ih alone does not explain higher input resistance, so a second change is needed
discriminating_measurement: ZD7288-sensitive sag, rebound and rest shift in both genotypes; Ih tail current and half-activation voltage; HCN1 surface vs total protein (biotinylation) and dendritic distribution; TRIP8b level
agents_or_tools: ZD7288 (HCN blocker), ivabradine and zatebradine (HCN blockers; ids not verified); HCN1/HCN2 and TRIP8b knockout lines as genetic controls
action: Block Ih in knockout slices and test whether rest, rebound and burst incidence fall
system_and_stage: Mouse neocortex and hippocampus; in an FCD rat model reduced Ih gave hyperpolarised rest, higher input resistance and less sag
benefit_sought: Identify whether Ih is a driver (blocker lowers bursting) or a brake
counter_evidence: In the FCD model reduced Ih increased excitability, so Ih can constrain network activity; blocking it in the knockout could worsen bursting. HCN1 gain-of-function DEE variants are epileptogenic (single genetic origin per variant)
falsifier: If ZD7288 does not remove the sag and rebound difference, H2 fails; a worse network outcome with block would indicate compensation, not refute Ih involvement

explanation: Developmental delay or altered cell size: immature neurons have high input resistance and a depolarised rest; knockout cells may be smaller or less mature (hypothesised)
assumes: Neuron maturation is slowed or morphology changed independent of channels
discriminating_measurement: Membrane capacitance, soma and dendrite reconstruction (biocytin, Sholl), age series P8-P30 of rest, Rin, sag; specific membrane conductance (Rin x area) in knockout vs wild type; GABA reversal potential and KCC2 level as maturation markers
agents_or_tools: Tools: biocytin fills; KCC2 immunostaining; no drug
benefit_sought: Decide whether the state is a stage-lagging cell and so whether channel pharmacology is premature
counter_evidence: A channel shift can coexist with normal size; heterozygote shares Rin change but only partly the rest and sag, which fits partial maturation lag less obviously
falsifier: If specific conductance and capacitance are equal across genotypes and the age curve matches, H3 fails
depth_and_source: Inferred; no source read for this knockout

explanation: Chronic bursting itself reshapes intrinsic properties (homeostatic or injury-like), so the membrane state is downstream of NMDA-receptor-driven network activity (hypothesised)
assumes: Intrinsic changes depend on activity history; NMDA-receptor-dependent bursts precede or drive them
discriminating_measurement: Record intrinsic properties with NMDA, AMPA and GABA-A receptors blocked and sodium channels blocked by TTX (synaptic isolation) in knockout vs wild type; chronic NMDA-receptor block in vivo or in slice culture before P13, then compare; compare bursting and non-bursting knockout slices (6 of 42 did not burst)
agents_or_tools: D-AP5, memantine and ifenprodil (GluN2B-selective; ids not verified), gap-junction tool carbenoxolone (source says bursts are also gap-junction dependent)
benefit_sought: Tells whether to treat the burst or the intrinsic state, and which is primary
counter_evidence: In the source preparation the bursts are NMDA-receptor and gap-junction dependent (observed in abstract); the same abstract reports depolarisation, so activity independence is untested here. Heterozygotes with 4 of 23 bursting already show the Rin change, which hints that intrinsic change need not need bursting
falsifier: If the rest shift and Rin change persist in synaptic isolation and in non-bursting slices, H4 as sole cause fails; a failure of NMDA block to remove them does not refute a role of bursting
depth_and_source: Observed: abstract of PMID 34634460 (the preparation); adjacent homeostasis: abstract of PMID 21123568, hippocampal culture and rat

explanation: Reduced tonic GABA-A conductance (fewer or weaker inhibitory inputs) lessens shunt, raising input resistance and depolarising rest (inferred)
assumes: Inhibitory tone is reduced in layer II/III; the source abstract reports lower IPSC frequency and amplitude, and hippocampal Wwox knockout lost interneurons
discriminating_measurement: Effect of gabazine or picrotoxin on holding current, rest and Rin in wild type vs knockout; ambient GABA, extrasynaptic delta-subunit currents; interneuron counts (PV, SST) in this cortex; chloride gradient (gramicidin perforated patch)
agents_or_tools: gabazine (SR-95531) and picrotoxin as probes; gaboxadol (THIP, delta-GABA-A agonist; id not verified) to restore tone
system_and_stage: Mouse neocortex P13-17 (proposed); hippocampus at 2 weeks for interneuron loss
benefit_sought: Finds a restorable inhibitory deficit that a GABAergic agent could address
counter_evidence: Hippocampal interneuron loss is a different region and a whole-body knockout (abstract only); neuron-specific deletion here may not reproduce it. Tonic-GABA contribution to rest is small in many cortical cells and depolarising GABA in immature cells reverses the sign
falsifier: If gabazine moves wild type to knockout values but does nothing in the knockout, H5 holds; if gabazine has equal effect in both, H5 is not the explanation
depth_and_source: Observed (abstract): PMID 34634460 and PMID 30290271; the mechanism is inferred

explanation: Membrane lipid or cholesterol change shifts gating or surface trafficking of HCN and K+ channels (hypothesised)
assumes: Neuronal Wwox loss changes membrane lipid composition enough to alter channels; no evidence found here that it does
discriminating_measurement: Cholesterol depletion or loading in slices (effect on sag and rest in wild type vs knockout); filipin staining; slice lipidomics; raft fractionation of HCN1
agents_or_tools: methyl-beta-cyclodextrin (cholesterol removal/loading tool) and mevastatin as used in heterologous HCN work (ids not verified)
system_and_stage: Human HCN1/2/4 in CHO cells (transferred); no neuron data read
benefit_sought: Test whether membrane lipids are a lever before drug choice
counter_evidence: In that heterologous work HCN1 mode-shifting was insensitive to cholesterol manipulation, while HCN2 and HCN4 were affected, so HCN1 may be a poor target for this lever; cell line, human isoforms
falsifier: If cholesterol manipulation changes neither genotype differently, H6 fails

explanation: Altered Na+/K+-ATPase electrogenic pump or energetic state depolarises rest (hypothesised)
assumes: Pump current contributes to rest at this stage; Wwox loss affects it directly or through metabolism
discriminating_measurement: Ouabain-sensitive current at low concentration, rest after pump block in both genotypes, ATP-dependence, intracellular sodium
agents_or_tools: ouabain (low concentration, tool), no repurposable agent proposed
benefit_sought: Rules a metabolic route in or out
counter_evidence: Targeted PubMed search for this link returned nothing (see queries); pump dysfunction usually raises, not lowers, input resistance only through other channels; no adjacent evidence retrieved
falsifier: If pump block depolarises both genotypes equally, H7 fails
depth_and_source: Not supported by any source reached; flagged as a low-prior filler
